question: If I work while I'm incarcerated, in a prison job or on work release, how is my pay set, what can the state deduct from my earnings and in what order, and what do I get back when I'm released?

gold_sections.why: Prison-industry pay: the Commissioner and the Chief Executive Officer of Maryland Correctional Enterprises set the compensation rate; regulations govern the method and time of payment.

Applies to State and local facilities: the Department collects earnings and pays room-and-board reimbursement (if required by law), support, restitution and victims compensation (20% of PIE earnings; 25% of other earnings while restitution is unpaid); balance paid within 15 days after release.

State work release: total earnings surrendered to the Division, the five-item order of priority for deductions, dependent support paid through local social services, balance credited and paid on release, final earnings forwarded within 15 days.

Each Division facility keeps a reserve account and a spending account for each incarcerated individual; the accounts may be charged for destroyed State property and medical fees, only under regulations that give due process first.
The medical visit fee (not to exceed $4 a visit in State facilities, with exceptions) that is the second work-release deduction and a permitted account charge.

Where MCE labor is used for open-market food, agriculture or seafood processing work, wages may not be less than local private-sector wages for similar work as determined by the Secretary of Labor; limited to minimum, prerelease and work-release security levels.

Road work for the State Highway Administration or a county or municipality: the employer pays the Division an agreed daily sum; the Division holds an amount to the worker's credit, pays it on release or discharge, and may pay dependents.

A court may enter a restitution earnings withholding order, including when the defendant is placed on work release; it ranks after child-support withholding orders; the default is 20% of earnings less other deductions required by law from work-release funds, capped by the federal Consumer Credit Protection Act.
Compliance with a judgment of restitution is a mandatory condition of work release; restitution is paid through the Department, which may add a collection fee of up to 2% of the judgment.

The Commissioner's annual report lists the job classifications and the daily wage scale at each prison for each job classification under the Division (the only statute on pay for ordinary institutional jobs).
The annual Maryland Correctional Enterprises report lists the MCE job classifications and the daily wage scale at each prison for each MCE job classification.
Release from a State facility: the Commissioner must adopt regulations for a release plan, including transportation from the facility on release (no statute sets a cash release payment).

nuggets.text: For prison-industry (Maryland Correctional Enterprises) work, the Commissioner of Correction and the MCE Chief Executive Officer set the pay rate, taking into account wage payments and incentives in other programs.
nuggets.quote: The Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer shall establish the compensation rate for incarcerated individual labor in Maryland Correctional Enterprises, taking into consideration other wage payments and incentives in other programs.

nuggets.text: When MCE labor is used for open-market food, agriculture or seafood-processing work (because State labor pools are diminished), the wages may not be less than private-sector wages for similar work in the same locality as determined by the Secretary of Labor, and only people at the minimum, prerelease and work-release security levels may do this work.
nuggets.quote: Wages paid to incarcerated individuals under subsection (b)(7) of this section may not be less than wages paid for similar work in the private sector of the same locality as determined by the Secretary of Labor. (3) Incarcerated individual labor under subsection (b)(7) of this section applies only to incarcerated individuals at the minimum, prerelease, and work release security levels.

nuggets.text: For road work, the State Highway Administration, county or municipality pays the Division of Correction an agreed daily sum, and the Division holds an amount it determines to the worker's credit, paid out on release or discharge.
nuggets.quote: shall hold an amount, as determined by the Division, to the credit of the incarcerated individual on whose account the payments were made

nuggets.text: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services collects the earnings of anyone in a State or local correctional facility and from them reimburses the county or State for food, lodging and clothing (if required by law), pays court-ordered dependent support, pays court-ordered restitution, and pays compensation for victims of crime.
nuggets.quote: The Department shall collect an incarcerated individual's earnings. (c) From an incarcerated individual's earnings, the Department shall: (1) if required by law, reimburse the county or State for the cost of providing food, lodging, and clothing to the incarcerated individual; (2) pay court ordered payments for support of dependents; (3) pay court ordered payments for restitution; and (4) pay compensation for victims of crime

nuggets.text: For people working in the federal Private Sector/Prison Industry Enhancement Certification Program, the Department withholds 20% of earnings for compensation for victims of crime.
nuggets.quote: the Department shall withhold 20% for compensation for victims of crime, in accordance with the requirements of the Program

nuggets.text: If you owe an unsatisfied judgment of restitution, the Department withholds 25% of your other (non-PIE) earnings for victims of crime until the judgment is satisfied.
nuggets.quote: (i) This paragraph applies to an incarcerated individual who is subject to an unsatisfied judgment of restitution. (ii) If an incarcerated individual has earnings that are not covered under the provisions of paragraph (1) of this subsection, the Department shall withhold 25% for compensation for victims of crime until the judgment is satisfied.

nuggets.text: Whatever remains after those payments is credited to your account, and the account balance must be paid to you within 15 days after you are released.
nuggets.quote: pay the balance in the incarcerated individual's account to the incarcerated individual within 15 days after the incarcerated individual is released

nuggets.text: On State work release you must turn over your total earnings to the Division of Correction, less payroll deductions required by law (such as taxes).
nuggets.quote: shall surrender to the Division the incarcerated individual's total earnings less any payroll deductions required by law

nuggets.text: The Division deducts from work-release earnings in a fixed order of priority: first, the cost to the State (as the Division determines) of your food, lodging and clothing; second, medical fees assessed under § 2-118.
nuggets.quote: The Division shall deduct from the incarcerated individual's earnings in the following order of priority: (i) an amount the Division determines to be the cost to the State of providing food, lodging, and clothing for the incarcerated individual; (ii) fees assessed under § 2–118 of this article;

nuggets.text: Third come your actual and necessary food, travel and other expenses while out on work release; fourth, support you are legally obligated to pay your dependents; fifth, court-ordered restitution.
nuggets.quote: (iii) the actual and necessary food, travel, and other expenses of the incarcerated individual when released from actual confinement under the work–release program; (iv) subject to paragraph (3) of this subsection, any amount that the incarcerated individual is legally obligated to pay to support the incarcerated individual's dependents; and (v) the amount that a court orders to be paid as restitution.

nuggets.text: Any balance left after the work-release deductions is credited to your account and paid to you on release.
nuggets.quote: Any balance that remains after the deductions are made under subsection (a) of this section shall be: (i) credited to the incarcerated individual's account; and (ii) paid to the incarcerated individual on release.

nuggets.text: In State correctional facilities the Secretary must charge a reasonable fee of no more than $4 for each visit to a medical unit, physician, dentist or optometrist; no fee may be charged for care required at intake or for the initial physical examination, care due to a referral by a nurse or physician's assistant, a follow-up visit initiated by a facility medical professional, necessary treatment, or care initiated by medical or mental-health staff.
nuggets.quote: This section applies to incarcerated individuals in a State correctional facility. (b) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection, the Secretary shall assess a reasonable fee not to exceed $4 for each visit by an incarcerated individual to a medical unit, physician, dentist, or optometrist for health care services.

nuggets.text: Each Division of Correction facility keeps two accounts for every incarcerated individual: a reserve account and a spending account.
nuggets.quote: A correctional facility in the Division shall maintain a reserve financial account and a spending financial account for each incarcerated individual in the correctional facility.

nuggets.text: Those accounts may be charged for the reasonable value of State property you destroy willfully, maliciously or through gross negligence, and for medical fees under § 2-118.
nuggets.quote: The accounts of an incarcerated individual may be charged for: (1) the reasonable value of any State property that the incarcerated individual: (i) willfully or maliciously destroys; or (ii) destroys as the result of gross negligence; or (2) any fees assessed under § 2–118 of this article.

nuggets.text: A court may enter an earnings withholding order for restitution (including when you are placed on work release); the standard amount is 20% of earnings less other legally required deductions from work-release funds, the court may order more if restitution is overdue, and the amount may not exceed the limits of the federal Consumer Credit Protection Act.
nuggets.quote: the payment amount under an earnings withholding order under this section is 20% of the earnings of a restitution obligor less other deductions required by law to be paid out of any funds earned under a work release plan. (2) If the restitution obligation of the restitution obligor is overdue, the court may impose a payment exceeding the amount allowed in paragraph (1) of this subsection. (3) (i) The amount of an earnings withholding order issued under this section may not exceed the limits of the federal Consumer Credit Protection Act.

nuggets.text: When a judgment of restitution has been entered, complying with it is a mandatory condition of any work release that is ordered or allowed.
nuggets.quote: compliance with the judgment of restitution: (i) may be a requirement in the judgment of conviction or disposition in a juvenile delinquency proceeding; (ii) if work release is ordered or allowed, shall be a condition of work release

nuggets.text: Restitution is paid to the Department, which may require the restitution obligor to pay an additional fee of up to 2% of the amount of the restitution judgment for the administrative costs of collection.
nuggets.quote: may require the restitution obligor to pay additional fees not exceeding 2% of the amount of the judgment of restitution to pay for the administrative costs of collecting payments or property

nuggets.text: Commissioner regulations decide what may be credited to or paid out of the reserve and spending accounts, and must give each incarcerated individual due process before an account is charged for destroyed property or medical fees.
nuggets.quote: The Commissioner shall adopt regulations that: (1) set forth those items that may be credited to or disbursed from an account under this section; and (2) set forth procedures for carrying out this section, including procedures that provide due process of law to each incarcerated individual before the incarcerated individual's accounts may be charged with a disbursement under subsection (b) of this section.

nuggets.text: No statute says who sets pay for ordinary Division of Correction (non-MCE) prison jobs; the Commissioner's annual report must state the job classifications for incarcerated labor and the daily wage scale at each prison for each job classification.
nuggets.quote: the job classifications for incarcerated individual labor in each department and facility under the authority of the Division; (5) the daily wage scale at each prison for each job classification under the authority of the Division

nuggets.text: If your final work-release earnings are needed for the required deductions, the balance of those earnings must be forwarded to you within 15 days after you are released from the Division's jurisdiction.
nuggets.quote: If any part of the incarcerated individual's final earnings under a work–release plan are required to satisfy the obligatory deductions set forth in subsection (b) of this section, the balance of those earnings shall be forwarded to the incarcerated individual within 15 days after the incarcerated individual's release from the Division's jurisdiction.

nuggets.text: Subject to federal law, earnings withholding orders are executed in this order: first child-support withholding orders under Family Law § 10-128, second restitution withholding orders, and last any other lien or legal process.
nuggets.quote: Subject to federal law, the order of priority of execution of an earnings withholding order is: (1) first, an earnings withholding order issued under § 10-128 of the Family Law Article; (2) second, an earnings withholding order issued under this section; and (3) lastly, any other lien or legal process.

nuggets.text: Dependent-support deductions from work-release pay are paid to your dependents through the local social services administration in the county where they live.
nuggets.quote: Any amount deducted under paragraph (1)(iv) of this subsection shall be paid to an incarcerated individual's dependents through the local social services administration in the county in which the dependents reside.

nuggets.text: The Commissioner must adopt regulations for a release plan from State facilities that helps identify resources after release, including transportation from the facility on release.
nuggets.quote: establishing a release plan for incarcerated individuals upon release from confinement in a State correctional facility to help identify resources to assist incarcerated individuals following release, including the provision of transportation from the facility for an incarcerated individual upon release

nuggets.text: The method and time of MCE pay are set by regulations the Commissioner adopts after Management Council review and any recommendation by the MCE Chief Executive Officer.
nuggets.quote: After review by the Management Council, and after consideration of any recommendation by the Chief Executive Officer, the Commissioner shall adopt regulations in accordance with Title 10, Subtitle 1 of the State Government Article that govern the method and time of compensation payments.

nuggets.text: The annual Maryland Correctional Enterprises report must list the MCE job classifications and the daily wage scale at each prison for each MCE job classification.
nuggets.quote: list the job classifications for incarcerated individual labor in each department and facility under the authority of Maryland Correctional Enterprises; (4) list the daily wage scale at each prison for each job classification under the authority of Maryland Correctional Enterprises

answer: No statute sets a dollar wage or who sets ordinary prison-job pay; the Commissioner yearly reports each prison's daily wage scale by job classification [N19]. For Maryland Correctional Enterprises jobs the Commissioner and MCE's chief executive set the rate [N1], regulations the payment method and timing [N24]. Open-market food or seafood work pays at least local private-sector wages [N2]; road-work pay is held for you [N3]. The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services collects earnings and pays required room-and-board reimbursement, court-ordered support, restitution and victims' compensation [N4]: 20% of Prison Industry Enhancement pay [N5], or 25% of other pay while you owe restitution [N6]. Work-release earnings minus payroll deductions go to the Division of Correction [N8], which deducts in order: the State's food, lodging and clothing cost; medical fees [N9] (up to $4 a visit [N12]); your food, travel and other expenses; dependent support, paid through local social services [N22]; then restitution [N10]. The statutes do not reconcile these lists [N4][N9]. Restitution compliance is a work-release condition [N16], plus a possible collection fee up to 2% of the judgment [N17]. A court restitution withholding order takes 20%, within federal limits, after child-support orders [N15][N21]. After due process, accounts may be charged for destroyed State property and medical fees [N13][N14][N18]. On release you get the work-release balance [N11]; final work-release earnings follow within 15 days of leaving Division jurisdiction [N20], account balances within 15 days of release [N7]. No statute provides release cash; release plans cover transportation [N23].

out_of_corpus.where: Code of Maryland Regulations (COMAR) Title 12, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (Division of Correction and Maryland Correctional Enterprises regulations adopted under Correctional Services 3-514 and 3-609)

out_of_corpus.what: The daily wage scale by job classification for ordinary institutional jobs and MCE jobs, inmate-account procedures, and what is provided at release (any release funds, clothing or transportation under the release plan)
out_of_corpus.where: Division of Correction directives and the annual reports under Correctional Services 3-207 and 3-509; release-plan regulations under Correctional Services 9-609

out_of_corpus.what: Private-sector prison industry work (PIECP): prevailing-wage pay and a cap on total deductions (room and board, family support, victim compensation, taxes) as a share of gross wages
out_of_corpus.where: 18 U.S.C. 1761(c) and the Bureau of Justice Assistance Prison Industry Enhancement Certification Program guideline

out_of_corpus.what: Payroll withholding on work-release wages (income tax, Social Security, Medicare) and the federal garnishment ceiling that caps restitution earnings withholding orders

local_option: People serving time in county detention centers fall under county-specific statutes rather than 3-804: each county's work release program (Correctional Services 11-702 through 11-725) sets its own deduction list, e.g. Calvert County (11-706) deducts food, lodging and travel costs to the county, then fines and costs, dependent support, and restitution, paying the balance on final release; the Baltimore City Detention Center program (11-704) caps the room-and-board deduction at one-third of net earnings and forwards final earnings within 15 days; regional correctional centers (11-319) let the center director make deductions; a county governing body decides whether county correctional-farm labor is paid and whether pay is given during confinement, withheld until release, or sent to dependents (11-407); Carroll County may pay the normal rate of pay and deduct the costs of employment and confinement (9-516); and a sentencing judge may let a person in a local facility keep or find a job paying a fair and reasonable wage (11-602).
notes: Scope is State prisoners (Division of Correction). Two statutory lists exist: 3-804(b) is the explicit 'order of priority' for State work release (food/lodging/clothing; 2-118 medical fees; work-release expenses; dependent support, paid through the local social services administration under 3-804(b)(3); restitution), and 9-615(c) applies to earnings of anyone in a State or local facility (reimbursement if required by law; support; restitution; victims compensation) without the phrase 'order of priority'. 9-615 reaches all earnings, including work-release pay, alongside the 3-804 order; the statutes do not say how the two interact. 3-804(b)(2) refers to deductions 'under subsection (a)'; read with (b)(1), the balance is what remains after the (b)(1) deductions. Two release-payout rules: the work-release balance is paid 'on release' (3-804(b)(2)) and, where final work-release earnings are needed for the deductions, the rest is forwarded within 15 days after release from the Division's jurisdiction (3-804(c)); the general account balance is paid within 15 days after release (9-615(e)(2)). 9-615(d)(3) and (d)(4) both govern the paragraph (1) PIE 20% withholding: it goes to the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund to pay restitution when restitution has been ordered, and is otherwise split 50/50 between the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund and the State Victims of Crime Fund; the statute names no destination for the 25% withheld under (d)(2). Criminal Procedure 11-617(b) ranks restitution earnings withholding orders after Family Law 10-128 child-support withholding orders and ahead of other liens. Correctional Services 4-307 makes restitution a condition of Patuxent Institution work release, as 11-607 does for work release generally. 9-504(d) (county road work) also has payments held to the individual's credit; 9-512(b)(2) lets the Division pay road-work earnings to needy dependents. 3-807(e)(1) lets an extended work-release plan (only for people sentenced for desertion or nonsupport of a spouse, child or destitute parent) direct earnings to family support and reimbursement of the State for room and board; it is left out of gold_sections as a narrow program. Work-release participants are not employees of the Division (3-805(a)). Injuries: a person injured in work for which a correctional facility paid wages or a stipulated sum may claim permanent-disability benefits from the Sundry Claims Board (Correctional Services 10-304) by the later of 12 months after release or 24 months after the injury (10-305(b)); PIE workers under MCE supervision are covered employees for workers' compensation (Labor and Employment 9-221(a)(2)), but no award is made until discharge by pardon, parole or expiration of sentence (Labor and Employment 9-607(a)); the Sundry Claims Board subtitle does not apply to injuries in private work-release employment (3-805(b)). No Maryland statute provides a cash release payment or release clothing; 9-609 requires release-plan regulations including transportation, and 9-609.1 requires an identification card (and, with written consent, a birth certificate and Social Security card) before release. Satisfactory work also earns diminution credit of 5 days a month (3-705), which is not pay. The Maryland Wage and Hour Law exemptions (Labor and Employment 3-403) do not mention incarcerated workers; prison employment is generally not covered employment for unemployment insurance (Labor and Employment 8-217). Family Law 12-104.1 stops child-support arrears from accruing during incarceration (and 60 days after) only for obligors not on work release with insufficient resources. Correctional Services 11-604 is not in the downloaded corpus.
